run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/fraud-detection since 2026-11-16T18:02:30Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/fraud-detection is explained by error status on fraud-detection's long-lived gRPC client stream to flagd: span 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' (span_kind SPAN_KIND_CLIENT) with rpc.grpc.status_code="4" (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) and durations of ~594–602 s. These are the only error-status spans the service produced in the observable telemetry, the matching flagd server spans are their children and record 'stream closed due to server-side timeout', and every observed EventStream span (10 of 10) ended in error, producing an error share of roughly 2.1–2.6% (12 STATUS_CODE_ERROR against 457 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans), the same magnitude as the alert's reported 0.0222. Pod-level health of fraud-detection (10/10 pods Running and Ready, restartCount 0, no termination reason, no failure events) and flagd resource usage (≈33 MB working set against GOMEMLIMIT 60MiB, zero CPU throttling) show no alternative fault. Two limits remain: the alert rule itself is not loaded in this Prometheus, and fraud-detection telemetry stops around 17:30 while the alert evaluation is stamped 18:02:30, so the alert's own evaluation and any baseline before ~17:11 could not be observed.

claims.text: The only error-status spans returned for service fraud-detection are on client span 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream': 10 spans with error=true, otel.status_code="ERROR", rpc.grpc.status_code="4" (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) and durations between 594,101,234 and 601,796,702 µs (≈9.9–10.0 minutes).

The matching flagd-side spans (service 'flagd', service_version v0.12.8, same operation 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream') are children of those fraud-detection client spans through supplied CHILD_OF parent references; two of them carry error=true with otel.status_description "stream closed due to server-side timeout" while seven record rpc.grpc.status_code="0".

The spanmetric series for service_name="fraud-detection" carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR only for 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' and 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt' (both SPAN_KIND_CLIENT); 'orders receive' and 'orders process' (SPAN_KIND_CONSUMER) have only STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and the 'resolve' client span likewise carries no error status. The same series carry 10 distinct exported_instance values.

The summed STATUS_CODE_ERROR counter for span_name 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' rose 1 → 3 → 6 → 7 → 10 between 17:22:00 and 17:24:30 and stayed at 10 through 17:32:00, while the duration histogram's +Inf count for the same operation equals 10, so every observed EventStream span ended in error status.

EventStream spans are long-lived: all 10 duration observations fall above the 15000 ms bucket (none in any bucket up to 15000 ms), consistent with the ~600 s durations seen in traces, whereas 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt' on the same service is fast (2 of 4 observations ≤800 ms, 4 of 4 ≤1000 ms) with no error increase.

In the observed minute-level window the raw span counters for service_name="fraud-detection" sum to 12 STATUS_CODE_ERROR against 457 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans (≈2.1–2.6% error share), the same magnitude as the alert's stated current value 0.02222222222222222.

Deployment otel-demo/fraud-detection reports spec.replicas 10, readyReplicas 10 and availableReplicas 10, and its 10 pods are owned by ReplicaSet fraud-detection-9fb7d885b, all phase Running with container fraud-detection ready=true, restartCount 0 and empty lastState, created between 17:06:32 and 17:09:35Z.

HorizontalPodAutoscaler fraud-detection has minReplicas 1 and maxReplicas 10 with currentReplicas 10, desiredReplicas 10 and condition ScalingLimited with reason TooManyReplicas, i.e. fraud-detection was scaled to its maximum of 10 replicas.

flagd runs 1 replica (readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1) in pod flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx, which is Running and Ready with 0 restarts and started 17:08:24Z; ReplicaSets show flagd-c47676d99 created 17:06:31Z with 0 replicas and flagd-58db7486bd created 17:08:24Z with 1 replica, i.e. flagd was rolled out around 17:06–17:08Z.

flagd's container showed no resource pressure while the stream errors occurred: container flagd memory working set was 32,538,624–34,258,944 bytes between 17:20 and 17:30 (GOMEMLIMIT env is 60MiB) and its rate of container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total was 0.

The fraud-detection deployment points at FLAGD_HOST=flagd and FLAGD_PORT=8013, and the flagd container starts as '/flagd-build start --port 8013 --ofrep-port 8016 --uri file:./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json'; no stream-timeout or deadline setting is visible in these specs.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) has every flag at defaultVariant "off" at query time (including kafkaQueueProblems, paymentFailure, adFailure, cartFailure, productCatalogFailure), so no injected fault flag was enabled in the visible flag configuration.

No warning or failure event names any fraud-detection pod: the namespace event list contains only HPA FailedGetResourceMetric/FailedComputeMetricsReplicas warnings for kafka, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping and valkey-cart (17:21–17:22Z), 61 'deployments/scale.apps "postgres" not found' warnings for postgres, and 'Killing' events for two recommendation pods at 17:22–17:23Z.

Error spans on checkout, frontend and frontend-proxy in the same window come from a different failure: checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' failed with otel.status_description 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to shipping service: Post "http://shipping:8080/get-quote": EOF' (rpc.grpc.status_code 13, HTTP 500 through frontend and frontend-proxy to the load-generator), a message that names shipping and not fraud-detection.

The observable fraud-detection telemetry does not reach the alert timestamp: span-metric range queries returned points only up to 17:30:38–17:32:00Z and the trace search returned fraud-detection spans only from 17:21:51 to 17:23:43Z (that trace view is flagged incomplete because the backend returned as many traces as requested), so the alert's 18:02:30Z evaluation lies outside the observable data.

Primary explanation for the alert: fraud-detection's flagd EventStream subscriptions are terminated after ≈600 s, each termination being recorded as a gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED error span on the client; because these are the service's only error spans and they amount to roughly 2.1–2.6% of its spans, the RequestErrorRate rule sees the 0.0222 error rate quoted in the alert.

Deeper cause candidate: the ~600 s stream cap is enforced by the flagd server, which closes the EventStream and reports 'stream closed due to server-side timeout'; the specific flagd setting or argument that imposes it is not visible in the deployment command (only --port, --ofrep-port, --uri) or in the flagd-config ConfigMap, so it could not be verified.

Alternative attribution that the remaining evidence cannot exclude: the ≈600 s limit is a client-side deadline in fraud-detection's flagd provider (FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013), in which case the periodic DEADLINE_EXCEEDED errors would originate in the fraud-detection deployment rather than in flagd. Mixed flagd server statuses (2 of 9 spans reporting the server-side timeout, 7 reporting rpc.grpc.status_code="0") are consistent with either side imposing the cap.

The erroring streams were opened by the pods created in the 17:06:32–17:09:35Z scale-up (deployment fraud-detection reached its HPA maximum of 10 replicas) and all reached the ≈600 s cap within a 2.5-minute burst at 17:22–17:24:30Z; whether pods that existed before that scale-up behaved the same cannot be determined, because no fraud-detection telemetry earlier than ~17:11 (traces) or ~17:20 (span metrics) is available.

Against attributing the failure to fraud-detection's own application logic: its flag-evaluation calls on the same dependency do not error (no error increase for 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt' or 'resolve'), and the terminating condition is recorded on flagd's server span as a server-side stream timeout, not on a fraud-detection server-side operation. Its consumer spans 'orders receive'/'orders process' carry no error status.

Rejected: pod-level failure of fraud-detection (crash, OOMKill, eviction, probe failure) as the cause of the error rate. All 10 pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and empty lastState (no termination reason), and no warning/failure event names any fraud-detection pod.

Rejected as far as observable: resource exhaustion in flagd (memory pressure against GOMEMLIMIT 60MiB or CPU throttling) driving the stream timeouts. Working set stayed at ~33 MB and the throttled-period rate was 0 throughout the observed interval.

Rejected: the checkout/frontend/frontend-proxy error spans in the same window as the cause of the fraud-detection alert. Their diagnostic text names a shipping failure (EOF from http://shipping:8080/get-quote) and no span in that failing trace involves fraud-detection or flagd.

gaps: The alerting rule 'RequestErrorRate' is not present in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules returned status no_data with no rules at all (evidence 9c283972-6d59-4272-8550-dfde8a990051-t0:0b3072ea-6cc3-4066-809f-be8222644a3c and 7ef14b8d-5302-4354-9ddb-cfa68f829f75-t0:ae07fc49-7914-49ef-9be4-1bc99c767474), so the alert expression, its evaluation window and its 18:02:30Z value could not be inspected or reproduced.

No fraud-detection or flagd telemetry covers 17:31–18:15:38Z (span-metric series end at 17:30:38–17:32:00Z and Jaeger's newest fraud-detection traces are from 17:23:43Z, the latter view incomplete), so it is unknown whether the EventStream DEADLINE_EXCEEDED errors continued or recurred at the alert timestamp of 18:02:30Z.

No baseline is available: Jaeger holds fraud-detection spans only from ~17:11 and span metrics only from ~17:20, so it cannot be stated whether this ~2.2% error share is newly elevated or a steady/preexisting condition.

Application logs could not be read: fetch_pod_logs returned status no_data for fraud-detection pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-2m24l (evidence 44fe1a4f-e46c-46a2-b7d7-cc4d9d2a06ef-t0:587bf9fe-1c50-42ac-b038-0d39984f8aff) and for flagd pod flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx (evidence 44fe1a4f-e46c-46a2-b7d7-cc4d9d2a06ef-t1:944c78ab-6940-4549-ba4e-81b9e13f767b), so the applications' own runtime messages about the stream closure are unknown.

It is unverified which side enforces the ≈600 s stream cap: the flagd command line and flagd-config ConfigMap show no stream-deadline setting, and fraud-detection's flagd provider configuration beyond FLAGD_HOST/FLAGD_PORT is not visible.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so any deployment, configuration or flag change at ~17:06–17:08Z could not be confirmed from change records (kube-state data shows a new fraud-detection ReplicaSet and a flagd rollout but not what was changed).
Whether the 10 failed streams reconnected and timed out again after 17:24:30Z is unknown: the EventStream error counter is flat at 10 through 17:32:00Z and there is no later data.
next_steps: Inspect the RequestErrorRate rule definition (and the Alertmanager/Prometheus instance that evaluates it) to confirm which metric, status filter and window produce 0.02222222222222222 for service_name="fraud-detection".

Check flagd's stream timeout configuration (flagd CLI/config for a stream deadline) and fraud-detection's flagd provider options to determine which side imposes the ≈600 s cap, and decide whether these long-lived stream terminations should count as request errors.
Compare the current fraud-detection error ratio against a period before the 17:06–17:08Z scale-up/rollout to confirm whether the EventStream DEADLINE_EXCEEDED errors are new or steady noise.
Review flagd and fraud-detection application logs (log ingestion returned no lines in this Run) for stream-close messages and reconnect behavior after 17:24:30Z.
Investigate the separate shipping-quote failure that produced checkout/frontend/frontend-proxy error spans in the same window, independently of this fraud-detection alert.
